Twenty comments

This is one of the tunes that follows “The Factory Girl” on Éilís Kennedy’s CD “Time to Sail.”

↳ Posted by slawlor@pobox.com on June 8th, 2005.

Cute tune…

Thanks for posting this…I remember learning this from Anna Massie at a fiddle workshop in Guelph when I was still quite wet behind the proverbial fiddle ears. It was promptly lost in tunes/months that followed.

↳ Posted by _Steph_ on June 9th, 2005.

John Williams

John Williams plays this on his new album “Raven.” When he talked about it at his concert he said he was in Louisiana trying to find something to play with the one row box players down there and thought of this one. When he played it for them they swore that it was a Cajun melody rather than an Irish barndance. The way he plays it definitely makes it have a Cajun sound.

↳ Posted by Musicalbison on March 9th, 2006.

X: 12 Denis Murphy’s Barndance

Transcription with variations based on the whistle playing, teaching & notations of John O’Brien/O’Briain, brother of fellow musicians, uileann pipes & whistles, Denis/Donncha and Mick/Michael…

The second part variations, the repeat with those short high D Crans ( ~d2 ), is from O’Brien’s approximation as inspired by the playing of Brendán & Cormac Begley… I similarly took to cranning those high e’s in that variation ( ~e2 )…

Another option given for the 3rd & 11th bars of that repeated second part -
| e3 g e z e2 |

↳ Posted by ceolachan on December 22nd, 2023.
